# Psychometric Digital Twin {.page-title}

[Behavioral ML research · UW–Madison]{.kicker}

## Overview

A study of whether classical machine learning or LLM-driven "digital twin" personas better predict a person's communication-apprehension score, and where each one is biased.

## What I built

- A behavioral prediction pipeline on 252 matched survey participants. Ridge, Elastic Net, k-NN, Random Forest, XGBoost, and MLP models predicted communication-apprehension scores from demographic, employment, geographic, and transit features, with cross-validation and SHAP feature importance.
- A check of the PRCA's psychometric structure with factor analysis.
- LLM "digital twin" personas with tiered embodiment prompts (OpenRouter/vLLM).
- A benchmark of the personas against the ML baselines on shared metrics (MAE, band accuracy, F1), plus an analysis of systematic bias by demographic group.
